summary: US-F2: The sale charges passed-on fees and records the breakdown, per channel
description:
**As** a buyer, **I want** the fees I actually pay to be visible on what I am buying, **so that**
the total I am charged is explainable line by line — and **as** an organizer, **I want** the fees I
absorb recorded even though the buyer never sees them.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-214

TKT-6's first COS: *every order line carries a fee breakdown; buyer-visible vs absorbed is correct
per channel*. This is the slice where fees become money.

**The trap this ticket exists to close:** `absorbed` and `passed_on` are not a display flag. A
passed-on fee increases what the card is charged; an absorbed fee does not, and yet must still be
recorded, because TKT-217 has to pay it to a payee out of money the buyer already paid. A build
that treats incidence as presentation charges the wrong total in one channel and cannot settle in
the other.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `ReservationCreate` accepts an optional channel code (opaque string, 1..100, ADR-024's exact
  shape). Absent = the default/public channel, which resolves NULL-channel fee rules only. The
  existing GA and seated request shapes stay valid — mind `minProperties`/`maxProperties`, which is
  how that schema expresses its XOR today.
- [ ] Commerce resolves fees through TKT-214's catalog read for the reserved ticket type **and
  channel**, with the same two failure classes the price path already distinguishes
  (`errResolveUnavailable` / `errResolveUnusable`). It **never degrades to "no fees"**: an
  unavailable or unusable fee resolution refuses the sale, exactly as an unusable price resolution
  does. "No rule matched" is a successful resolution with an empty fee set and must not be
  conflated with either failure.
- [ ] The breakdown is computed in **integers only** (ADR-001): per-ticket and per-order fixed
  bases, and a percentage base as basis points with **checked** multiplication and the rounding
  direction the TKT-214 ADR documents. No float anywhere on the path.
- [ ] `passed_on` fees increase the reservation's `total_amount`; `absorbed` fees do not change
  what the buyer pays. **Both** appear in the breakdown. A test proves two reservations differing
  only in channel — same base price, same fee amount, opposite incidence — charge different totals
  and record the same fee amount.
- [ ] The reservation persists a fee snapshot with the same discipline as
  `price_resolution_snapshot` (migration 0006): the resolution document **verbatim** plus the
  computed breakdown, snapshot-not-reference, the storability guard applied **before** the hold
  exists, nullable and not backfilled, with the shape pinned by a DB-level CHECK.
- [ ] The `Reservation` response carries the breakdown (per fee code: code, basis, incidence,
  amount, currency) and splits `amount` into face value and passed-on fees. It must be **optional**
  in the contract, not required — every pre-existing reservation response lacks it and ADR-028
  fails closed, so requiring it would turn valid responses into 500s. Regen committed.
- [ ] Any total that would exceed the contract's `Money` bound is refused **before** inventory
  commits — a 4xx, never a 500 with an orphan hold. The existing `quantity < 1 ||
  amount > MaxInt64/quantity` guard moves with the arithmetic, it does not get left behind on the
  price-only path.
- [ ] Checkout charges the reservation's stored `total_amount` unchanged. **Exactly one place**
  computes the fee — recomputing at capture is the divergence bug ADR-036 names for prices.
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code committed before the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** payees and splits (TKT-216) · the settlement ledger (TKT-217) · fee behaviour on
refund, exchange and cancellation (carved out to a follow-up; see the epic readiness verdict) ·
storefront display of the breakdown (the response carries it; rendering is TKT-2/TKT-17 work).

objective.note: A sale charges the right total per channel and records a fee breakdown that TKT-217 can settle from.

scope.note: Commerce only, reserve + checkout. Snapshot, breakdown, incidence, channel. No payees, no ledger, no post-purchase.

uncertainties.note: Whether per-order fixed fees are apportioned across lines or carried once on the reservation - today a reservation is one ticket type, so it may be moot; the plan states which and why. Rounding unit comes from TKT-214's ADR, not from this plan.

dependencies.note: Blocked by TKT-214: this ticket consumes its resolution contract and its ADR's rounding rule.

approach.note: Mirror services/commerce/internal/api/catalog_pricing.go end to end: one read, strict-semantics/tolerant-fields decode, storableSnapshot before the hold, validate() before use. Extend rather than fork - two near-identical consumer files is how one of them stops being maintained.

first_slice.note: The money path is the COS; everything else in the epic reads what it writes.

success.note: Charged-total assertions and snapshot-shape assertions; the incidence proof is a differential test across two channels.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

governingAdrs.why: SHIPPED BY TKT-214 AND THIS TICKET'S DIRECT INPUT. Fixes the fee model: three basis kinds as a database-enforced tagged union (per_ticket_fixed / per_order_fixed / percentage_bps), FLOOR rounding AT THE INDIVIDUAL TICKET with checked multiplication before the divide (§2 - this ticket implements that arithmetic; catalog never multiplies), passed_on vs absorbed incidence and what each does to the charged total (§3), exact-match channel semantics with NULL meaning channel-agnostic and an omitted channel NOT being a wildcard (§4), catalog-resolves/commerce-computes ownership with ADR-002 unamended (§5), the /internal/ read and its X-Internal-Token guard (§6), and - easy to miss - §2's rule that A RESOLVED FEE OF AMOUNT 0 IS STILL A RESOLVED FEE and must appear in the breakdown.

The pricing model ADR-046 extends. Relevant here for §2's integer-safety requirement and for the precedent that commerce consumes catalog's resolved number and NEVER recomputes it - two places computing one number is a divergence bug waiting for its first mismatch.
Money is integer minor units + ISO-4217. Every fee computation on this ticket is integer-only with a checked multiplication; no float, no big.Float, no decimal-as-string round trip.

Commerce owns 'pricing/fee/promo evaluation' - the arithmetic is this service's job. Catalog owns the rules. ADR-046 §5 deliberately did NOT move that line, so this ticket must not push arithmetic back into catalog.
Contract-first: ReservationCreate and Reservation changes must be declared in services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml and the generated code committed BEFORE the gate.

Response validation fails closed. A new REQUIRED response field turns every pre-existing valid response into a 500 - which is why the breakdown must be optional in the contract, exactly as Reservation.seats had to be.

The checkout journal protocol: what commerce may do before and after the hold exists. A failure AFTER inventory commits leaves an orphan hold and a 500 for the buyer, which is why TKT-153 moved the snapshot storability check to before the hold. Same discipline applies to the fee snapshot.
The claim runs in one Postgres transaction and is the correctness boundary. Nothing here may make the claim conditional on a second network read completing after the hold.

Checkout recovery REPLAYS a checkout whose outcome is unknown. A total recomputed on replay from a re-resolved fee set would drift from the total the buyer authorised; only the stored total may be charged.
Channel codes are exact opaque strings, 1..100 chars, NULL = default/public. Inventory already stores one on claims. There is no registry; do not invent one.

SAME-WEEK ADR, included by the TKT-214 retro rule rather than by area match - and it is the one that governs how commerce reaches catalog's new /internal/ route. Declared security: guards a service's PUBLIC contract; an inline check guards its internal surface. Commerce already holds catalog's internal token and calls /internal/ticket-types/{id} with it (server.go:1158, internal=true) - the fee read takes the SAME credential, so this adds no blast radius.
Same-week-adjacent: the PSP port boundary. The captured amount is what the provider confirmed; the fee breakdown must reconcile to it, not to a recomputation.

reference.summary: Epic lineage and the three epic-level COS
The fee model, shipped and merged - read §2 (rounding), §3 (incidence), §4 (channel), §9 (a considered code with a null winner)

The read this ticket consumes: GET /internal/ticket-types/{id}/fee-resolution?channel_code=... , X-Internal-Token, 401. Winner is NULLABLE - a code every rule of which is outside its window resolves with winner:null and must be skipped, not treated as a fee of zero
The consumer to mirror end to end: one read, strict-semantics/tolerant-fields decode, storableSnapshot BEFORE the hold, validate() before use, two failure classes that never degrade to a default
The reserve path, the EUR-only limitation, and how commerce sends the internal credential (call(..., internal=true))
The snapshot precedent: nullable, not backfilled, CHECK-shaped, Down refuses to drop with data present
ReservationCreate's minProperties/maxProperties XOR - adding an optional property changes those counts and the XOR must still hold
TKT-214 closeout: the two agent-made decisions this ticket inherits (the forced/channel inversion, and the /internal/ route)
